## Authoritative Sources and Adaptation

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Authority** | Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard and Qwen |
| **Model** | [open source](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B) |
| **Evaluator** | [open source](https://github.com/ShishirPatil/gorilla/tree/main/berkeley-function-call-leaderboard) |

**Adaptation boundary:** The max runner uses pinned Transformers for laptop inference, reproduces BFCL's Qwen FC prompt and parser, scores all six complete categories with the byte-pinned official AST checker, and applies the official equal-weight Non-Live AST aggregation.

## How to Run

```bash
# one-time asset preparation
uv run mlperf fetch --workload function-calling --profile max

# benchmark run (writes JSON/HTML/CSV reports + .provd provenance)
uv run mlperf run --workload function-calling --profile max --open-report

# quick smoke pass
uv run mlperf run --workload function-calling --profile min

# research envelope
uv run mlperf run --workload function-calling --profile pro
```

See the [running guide](../../guide/running.qmd) for profile semantics, report handling, and power measurement flags.

**Reviewer notes:**

- The target is the official BFCL V4 Qwen3-1.7B Non-Live AST summary.
- The max runner binds all 1,150 cases, exact model bytes, the official Qwen FC prompt and parser, and the official AST checker.
- The deterministic evaluator self-check retains three known Java representation exceptions; they do not remove tasks from model scoring.
